Beat l6-more (with l6-year, l6-rohan, l6-sharma2): 'That is more than Rohan spends in a whole year, even at ₹40,000 a month. The money now earns more than the life costs' compares year-20 nominal growth (₹12.0 L at 8% on ₹1.50 Cr) with TODAY's spending. By the video's own 6% inflation (l1-trap, l5-honest) the same life costs about ₹1.28 L a month, ~₹15.4 L a year, by year 20, so the growth does NOT cover it; and spending all 8% growth while prices rise 6% shrinks the pot in real terms (real growth ~2%, before tax). The conclusion the numbers do not support (rule 3), and Rohan 'the job becomes optional' / Sharma 'That is the idea' builds on it. Fix: compare like with like: add a price_rise maths for ₹40,000 at 6% over 20 years and show the year-20 cost next to the growth, or move the comparison to today's money (real_return), or make the level-6 pot large enough that its growth covers the year-20 cost and say a sustainable draw is well below the full nominal return; reword l6-more so it is true under the stated assumptions.

Note (not a reject): open beat says the same month 'will cost ₹71,634' as a certainty; better 'at 6% inflation, could cost' (l1-trap already words it as an assumption). l3-down 'The cushion goes into the card' sits oddly with 15 years of minimums; l3/l3-fork omit 18% GST on card interest and EMI-conversion processing fees (both make the minimum road worse, so not misleading). FD at 7%: SBI general-public top rate is 6.80% (5-10y 6.05%), within the channel's 6-7.5% band; 6% inflation fits Sept 2026 CPI 5.54% (MoSPI). 3.5%/month and 5% minimum due match issuer MITCs (Bajaj/IndusInd 3.5%, IndusInd MAD 5%). Beats l6-year/l6-more/l6-catch with l6-rohan/l6-sharma2 (re-review): the like-for-like comparison is now right (₹24.0 L growth on ₹3 Cr at 8% vs ₹15,39,425 a year of life in year 20 at 6%), but l6-catch's remedy contradicts the video's own numbers. Spending ₹15.4 L of the ₹24.0 L leaves ₹8.6 L, while keeping ₹3 Cr level with 6% inflation needs ₹18 L a year. So 'spend less than the full growth, and let the rest keep up with prices' is impossible at this pot, the pot shrinks in real terms every year, and 'the job becomes optional?' / 'That is the idea' is still not supported (rule 3). The real return is about 2% (8% vs 6%), so a pot whose growth covers the bill AND keeps up with prices needs about ₹15.4 L / 0.02 = ~₹7.7 Cr (before tax). Fix: either raise the rich pot to about ₹8 Cr (say ₹8,00,00,000: ₹64 L growth, ₹48 L to keep up with prices, ₹16 L left > ₹15.4 L bill) and keep the lines, or keep ₹3 Cr and reword l6-more/l6-catch/l6-sharma2 honestly (the growth covers the bill for now, but to also keep up with prices the pot must be far bigger, so level six is a direction, not a finish line), with no 'job becomes optional' / 'That is the idea' endorsement at ₹3 Cr.
